sections.history: Thirumittakode, in Palakkad district beside the Bharathapuzha, is the Divya Desam that the Alvar hymns call Thiruvithuvakkodu. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvar saints in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Malai Nadu, the Kerala country. Its singer was Kulasekhara Alvar, the Chera prince whose Perumal Thirumozhi is part of the Prabandham, and who is usually placed in the ninth century. The Lord is worshipped as Uyyavanda Perumal, also called Abhaya Pradhan, with the Goddess Vithuvakkottu Valli, also known as Padmapani Nachiyar. The temple is popularly known as the Anchumoorthi Temple, the temple of five deities, because a Shiva shrine stands at the same site and the place is associated with both Vishnu and Shiva. The Pandavas, too, are remembered here.
sections.architecture: The temple lies on the bank of the Bharathapuzha and is distinguished by its plan: four Vishnu sannidhis face the four directions, so that the Lord is seen in every direction, while a Shiva shrine stands within the same site. This gives the precinct the sense of a gathering of five presences that the popular name Anchumoorthi recalls. The names of the vimana and the tank are not firmly recorded, so none is given here.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of King Ambarisha, devoted to Vishnu, whom the sage Durvasa once wronged and then, repenting, blessed. Ambarisha asked that the Lord appear to him in his Vyuha form, visible in all four directions, and the four Vishnu sannidhis facing the four directions are remembered as the answer to that prayer. One tradition adds that Ambarisha attained moksha here. Sources differ on the Pandavas: they are also remembered at this shrine, though who built it is held differently by different accounts.
sections.festivals: Thiruvonam is observed here, and Vaikunta Ekadashi is kept as the most sacred day of the Vaishnava year. As the temple honours both Vishnu and Shiva, devotees of both traditions come. Dates follow the temple’s own calendar, so confirm locally before planning a visit around them.
sections.experience: A riverside Divya Desam that rewards the pilgrim who takes time to stand before each of the four Vishnu sannidhis in turn, and to see the Shiva shrine. Those who know Kulasekhara Alvar’s Perumal Thirumozhi may like to read its verses here, where the Chera prince’s devotion is remembered. Enjoy the calm of the Bharathapuzha bank.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions, usually with a midday closure; festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirumittakode is in Palakkad district on the Bharathapuzha, reached by road from Pattambi and Shoranur, which are the usual railheads for the area; autorickshaws and taxis serve the short road journey. Kozhikode and Kochi are the airport gateways. Confirm local transport in advance.
